item.title: Police confirm rescue of 3 kidnapped Zamfara Islamic clerics
item.description: The Zamfara Commissioner of Police, CP Muhammad Bello, has confirmed the rescue of three of the six Islamic Clerics (Imam) kidnapped on September 12, while travelling to Talata Mafara, Zamfara. Bello gave the confirmation in an interview with some select reporters on Friday in Gusau. He said the rescue followed a multi-agency collaboration and seamless synergy between the Office of the National Security Adviser (ONSA), the Department of State Services (DSS) and police operatives. The CP said security tactical operations remained ongoing in full force, leveraging real-time intelligence supplied by local community members to track down the remaining armed bandits and ensure the safe rescue of the three clerics still in captivity. The News Agency of Nigeria (NAN) reports that the ONSA, in a high-stakes intelligence-driven collaboration with the DSS and the Nigeria Police Force (NPF), rescued the three Islamic clerics kidnapped while en route to a special prayer session for President Bola Tinubu in Talata Mafara, Zamfara. NAN also reports that the victims were part of a group of six Islamic clerics abducted on Sept. 12, when heavily armed bandits intercepted them around 11:30 a.m. on the Dakko-Damri feeder road near Sububu Forest in Bakura Local Government Area. The clerics, identified as Imam Yahuza, Magawata Abdullahi, Malam Shehu Dakko, Imam Bala Fagon and Na’ibi Tasi’u, were travelling to Talata Mafara to attend a special prayer gathering to seek divine favour for Tinubu’s administration. Their abductors had reportedly demanded N30 million ransom for their release. A senior security operative involved in the extraction also confirmed that the three clerics were rescued unhurt following meticulous, intelligence-led manoeuvres. NAN learnt that the clerics are said to be in stable condition after receiving medical evaluation and expert debriefing. The security operatives confirmed that the three clerics were slated for formal handover to the Zamfara Government to reunite them with their families. The Police command assured that operational leads would continue, urging the public to maintain a vigilant flow of timely, actionable information to help flush out terrorist elements across the region. (NAN) The post Police confirm rescue of 3 kidnapped Zamfara Islamic clerics appeared first on Vanguard News .

item.title: Sowore, police differ over attack in Ekiti
item.description: Omoyele Sowore, presidential candidate of the African Action Congress (AAC), and the Ekiti State Police Command have given conflicting accounts of an incident at a restaurant in Ado-Ekiti, Ekiti State, on Friday. While Sowore insisted that he and members of his team were violently attacked, the police described the incident as an altercation with some individuals, saying the activist sustained a minor injury. The Police Public Relations Officer, Sunday Abutu, said the command received an alert that Sowore was having issues with some individuals at a restaurant in Ado-Ekiti and immediately deployed operatives to the scene. Abutu said the operatives rescued the AAC presidential candidate and took him to the Police Hospital, Ado-Ekiti, where he was receiving treatment. However, Sowore, in a statement published on his social media accounts, rejected the police description of the incident as an “altercation”. “There was no altercation! We were attacked!” he declared. He accused the Ekiti State Police Command and the Department of State Services (DSS) of attempting to suppress evidence relating to the incident. Sowore alleged that security operatives seized CCTV footage from the restaurant where the incident occurred, claiming that the attackers were captured on camera and accusing the agencies of attempting to shield those responsible. He also faulted the state Commissioner of Police, CP Falade Adegoroye Michael, for describing the incident as an altercation, saying the police commissioner had visited the scene and seen the injuries sustained by the victims but subsequently played down their severity. Sowore further alleged that DSS operatives had been trailing and harassing him since his arrival in the state on Thursday. He claimed that the operatives also threatened the manager of a restaurant where he and his team had earlier eaten, warning him against allowing them to use the premises again. He said the attack occurred shortly after he concluded an interview at MIDAS FM 90.5 in Ado-Ekiti on Friday. Sowore also alleged that some of the attackers came from the Ekiti State Government House and received operational support from DSS operatives. Police Response The police, however, denied reports that the activist was kidnapped, following a social media post claiming that he had been seized by armed thugs and his whereabouts were unknown. Abutu said in a statement that the command wished to clarify that Sowore was not kidnapped but was rescued by police operatives after they received information about the incident. “The command wishes to categorically clarify that Mr. Sowore was not kidnapped. Rather, preliminary information indicates that he had an altercation with some individuals at a restaurant in Ado-Ekiti, following which the police were immediately alerted. “Upon receiving the report, police operatives swiftly mobilised to the scene and successfully rescued him. He, however, sustained a minor injury and is currently receiving medical attention at

item.title: Some called him warlord, but he was liberator, pan-Africanist – Yormie Johnson’s widow
item.description: By Dickson Omobola Speaking about Liberia’s democratic evolution without mentioning the late Prince Yormie Johnson, better known as PYJ, would be a disservice to history. Although Johnson died on November 28, 2024, at the age of 72, he transitioned from being an officer in the Armed Forces of Liberia to becoming a democrat, senator and two-time presidential candidate. Hailing from Nimba County, the second-most populous county in Liberia, Johnson wielded considerable influence over the county’s politics, operating as a key kingmaker and political deal-broker. His support was instrumental in the emergence of presidents. His political protégé is the current Vice President of Liberia, Jeremiah Kpan Koung Sr. In this exclusive interview, the late PYJ’s widow, Mrs Amira Johnson, during a recent visit to Nigeria, shares insights into life without her husband, and struggles for the liberation of his people, describing him as a pan-Africanist. She also calls on African leaders to remain united in the interest of the continent. Excerpts: How has your experience been so far, and what has impressed you most about the country since your arrival? Well, Nigeria is like a second home to me and my family. If you could recall, my husband and I settled here briefly during the time of the crisis in Liberia. My husband was moved here by the Economic Community of West African States, ECOWAS, and we stayed here and nurtured our children for 14 years. When the political atmosphere became stable, we had to go back and my husband contested to be a senator. So, my experience here has been so wonderful. Before now, I had come, but since my husband passed, this is my first time coming. Also, I came to SCOAN, which is my major reason for coming. I came to meet with the woman of God, Pastor Mrs TB Joshua. She and the late prophet TB Joshua had been our spiritual parents before my husband passed. While we lived in Nigeria for 14 years, that was where we used to fellowship and we went back to Liberia where we used to come from time to time. But since the prophet passed away and my husband passed on, this is my first experience. It has been wonderful. She received me warmly at the church. She hosted me. She is like a family. She welcomed me and we spent quality time visiting the mountains, doing spiritual work, praying for Liberia, praying for myself, my family and for peace and stability in the world in general. Prophet TB Joshua died five years ago. Given that you had not visited SCOAN since his passing, did you notice any change about the church? I must admit, I was quite impressed with the church. Nothing has changed. Pastor Mrs Evelyn Joshua, I must give it to her. In Liberia, we say she is a double person. She is two. We call them in my tradition, man-woman. She is a strong woman. What a woman. She is holding the church together. As a guest, I lodged in the church. The food, the workers, everything is in the same standard. Nothing has dropped beneath the standard they maint

item.title: The Signal: INEC Draws The Line, The Politicians Must Now Face The Voters
item.description: An important decision on governorship candidates, fresh pressure over the voters’ register, and a new battle for the South-East have shifted the 2027 campaign into more consequential territory. The politicians are still negotiating power. The electoral commission is beginning to determine who can contest it. For weeks, Nigeria’s political conversation has revolved around familiar questions. Who is supporting President Bola Tinubu? Can Atiku Abubakar and Peter Obi agree on a common strategy? How much influence does Nyesom Wike command? Which governor will deliver which state? Then, on Friday, the Independent National Electoral Commission (INEC) reminded everyone that there is another player in this election: the umpire. INEC announced the outcome of its review of complaints arising from the exclusion of governorship and state assembly candidates. Some politicians received welcome news. Others discovered that their appeals had failed. Among the most notable decisions, former Communications Minister Isa Pantami succeeded in his petition concerning the Gombe governorship election, although his candidacy remains subject to pending litigation. Ladi Adebutu, the PDP’s governorship candidate in Ogun State, was less fortunate. His petition was rejected. These decisions may appear to be administrative matters. They are not. They affect the choices available to voters, the calculations of political parties, and potentially the balance of power in important states. And they arrive at a moment when INEC is already facing intense scrutiny over the integrity of the voters’ register. The emerging question is no longer simply which politician has the strongest campaign organisation. It is whether Nigeria’s electoral institutions can apply the rules consistently, resolve disputes transparently and command public confidence when the votes are counted. Pantami gets a reprieve. Adebutu does not. INEC’s latest decisions offer a revealing picture of the difficulties political parties are experiencing with the Electoral Act and candidate nomination procedures. The commission received 69 petitions from 12 political parties across 26 states concerning governorship nominations. Of those, 41 succeeded, and 28 were rejected. For state assembly elections, 25 of the 61 petitions were successful, while 36 were rejected. The figures tell us something important. This is not an isolated disagreement involving one or two politicians. It is a substantial problem affecting party nominations across the country. The disputes concern membership registers, compliance with statutory deadlines, alleged multiple nominations and the wrongful inclusion or exclusion of candidates. INEC says it examined the complaints against relevant records and legal provisions. In Gombe, Pantami’s successful petition offers the PDP an opportunity to compete with a candidate whose exclusion had threatened its position in the state. But the pending court proceedings mean that the matter is not entirely settled

item.title: 46-yr-old businessman commits suicide, leaves video message for family
item.description: By Dayo Johnson, Akure A 46-year-old businessman, Akinbolusere Kayode, has reportedly died by suicide in Ondo Town, Ondo State. Sources said he took his life in his office near BOVAS Petrol Station in Igba Town at about 3 p.m. on Thursday. Two empty bottles suspected to have contained poisonous substance were recovered by police detectives attached to the Bolorunduro Division who visited the scene. According to sources, the deceased recorded a video in which he spoke about his business challenges, humble beginnings, and relationship with his wife, whom he praised for standing by him throughout his struggles. He also repeatedly stated that no one pressured him into deciding to transfer his properties to his wife and three children. The state Police Public Relations Officer, DSP Jimoh Abayomi, confirmed the incident. Abayomi said the two empty bottles suspected to have contained Sniper insecticide were recovered from a nearby bush during the police investigation. He added that preliminary findings indicated that the deceased recorded a video before his death in which he lamented the hardships he faced in life. The video has since circulated widely on social media. His remains were evacuated and deposited at the State Hospital morgue for preservation and further examination. Police said no signs of foul play or visible injuries were observed on the body during the initial examination. The Commissioner of Police in the state, Felix Ohagwu, has ordered a thorough investigation into the circumstances surrounding the incident to determine the actual cause of death. Ohagwu urged members of the public to refrain from speculation and allow investigators to carry out their work. He also advised individuals experiencing emotional distress, marital difficulties, or other personal challenges to seek timely support and assistance rather than resorting to actions that could endanger their lives. item.title: ‘Why I strangled, mutilated Adedotun Oluwaseun’ – Murder suspect who mourned with victim’s family
item.description: By Evelyn Usman For the family of Mrs Adedotun Oluwaseun, retirement was supposed to usher in a season of peace, rest and the joy of reaping the fruits of years of dedicated service. Instead, the death of their beloved mother has left them grieving and grappling with painful questions about the circumstances surrounding her final hours. Read Also: Police arrest suspect over murder of Adedotun Oluwaseun , retired Ogun teacher The retired confidential secretary with the Ogun State Universal Basic Education Board was allegedly strangled and repeatedly slashed with a machete in her residence at Bode Olude community, Abeokuta, Ogun State. A home that should have offered her security became the scene of a violent death, leaving her family searching for answers. Nearly eight months after the incident, the Ogun State Police Command announced a breakthrough with the arrest of 49-year-old Saburi Lateef, a popular transporter in Abeokuta, also known as Alhaji Oki Osan. In a disturbing twist, the suspect was reportedly among those who visited the deceased’s residence to commiserate with her family after her death, according to police sources. Investigation A source in the Homicide Section of the Ogun State Police Command, who spoke on condition of anonymity, said investigators initially had no clear lead to the perpetrator. According to the source: “At the beginning, there was no link to the perpetrator of the act, but the Commissioner of Police, CP Olubode Ojajuni, directed that we should ensure that we do everything possible to unravel the killers.” Police sources alleged that Lateef gained access to the deceased’s residence while she was away attending a retirement party organised for a friend around the Rounder area of Abeokuta. “He was ransacking the whole place when the woman returned. In his bid to prevent being exposed, he strangled the woman. “Not convinced that the woman was dead, he picked a cutlass and inflicted multiple cuts on her body. After that, he picked up her body and took it to the toilet, where he placed it on the closet to confirm if she was actually dead. “He spent more than an hour carrying out the act without attracting the attention of other residents in the neighbourhood,” the source alleged. ‘I don’t know what came over me’ — Suspect In his account, Lateef attributed his alleged action to frustration over the money he claimed Oluwaseun was keeping for him. He said: “I don’t know what came over me that day. She was owing me N3.45 million, being the proceeds of my truck, which I sold as scrap. I have known Big Mummy (the deceased) for about 10 years now. I knew her since when her building was under construction, but it was when she moved in that we became close. “It all started last year, when my truck broke down. I couldn’t get enough money to repair it. So, I parked it somewhere around my area in Bode Olude. After some time, some people came to buy it. “Before then, I had told Big Mummy (the deceased) that I needed a loan to buy

item.title: ‘I cry, break down behind closed doors’ – Funke Akindele reflects on pressures of being in the spotlight
item.description: By Aiyedun Oluwadamilola Nollywood actress and producer Funke Akindele has opened up about her emotional struggles behind the cameras, revealing that she sometimes cries and breaks down in private despite her cheerful public image. The actress made this known during an interview with CNN, where she reflected on the pressures of fame, public scrutiny of her relationships and the importance of prioritising personal well-being. “I cry. I lock myself in the room, cry, break down, and hit the bed. But I just pick myself up and come back to life,” Akindele said. The filmmaker, popularly associated with her ability to entertain audiences through her films and public appearances, acknowledged that the cheerful image people see does not always reflect what she experiences privately. She also spoke about the effect of public opinion on her personal life, recalling moments when she questioned her decisions and worried about how people would judge her. “Sometimes I tell myself, you’ve made a mistake again. How are people going to judge you?” she said, describing the thoughts she sometimes had to overcome. Akindele explained that she has gradually learnt to confront challenges and move forward rather than allow public opinion to determine how she sees herself. Beyond dealing with criticism, the actress highlighted the importance of self-care and maintaining relationships with loved ones while pursuing professional success. item.title: Taraba: Day bandits killed 62, injured 52, dislodged 7,123
item.description: • We can no longer farm, they took everything away from us — survivor By Femi Bolaji, Jalingo Friday, October 23, 2026, began like any other market day in Binnari, a rural community in Karim-Lamido Local Government Area of Taraba State, where the life of the people revolves around farming, fishing, livestock rearing and cross border trade. Read Also: Death toll in Taraba bandits’ attack now 50 From the early hours, residents and traders from neighbouring communities were busy going about their daily activities. Farmers brought their produce to market, food sellers prepared for customers, and livestock owners hoped to make sales that would help sustain their families. For many, the market was more than a place to buy and sell. It was where household needs were met, school fees were raised, debts were settled and plans for the coming week were made. But before the day ended, that familiar routine had been violently interrupted. Armed bandits on motorbikes reportedly stormed the community, opening fire on people going about their business, killing residents, destroying property and looting stores. In the confusion that followed, families fled for safety, leaving behind homes, belongings and livelihoods they had spent years building. By the time the immediate danger had passed, Binnari had been left counting its losses. Casualties The National Emergency Management Agency (NEMA), in it’s preliminary reports from the Taraba State Emergency Management Agency (TSEMA) and posted on its official social media handles put the death toll at 62. Another 52 people were reported injured, while 5,187 residents were displaced and 7,123 people affected by the attack. The figures, contained in a statement issued by NEMA on October 27, 2026, followed an on-the-spot assessment by TSEMA’s Executive Secretary, Dr. Echuseh Audu. Behind those numbers are families struggling to understand how a day that began with ordinary hopes ended in death, displacement and uncertainty. For the people of Binnari, the tragedy is not simply about the number of lives lost. It is also about the children whose education may have been interrupted, the farmers who have lost their livestock, the traders who can no longer return to the market with confidence and the families now wondering how to begin again. In a community where people depend largely on what they produce, catch, rear or sell, the attack has threatened not only lives but the very means through which residents survive. Binnari’s market has long served as an important meeting point for people from different communities and neighbouring states like Plateau, Gombe and Bauchi. Farmers come with grain and other agricultural produce. Fishermen bring their catch, while livestock owners and traders gather to exchange goods and negotiate prices. For many residents, market day offers an opportunity to earn money, replenish household supplies and reconnect with people they may not have seen for days or weeks. Such exchanges have helped sust

item.title: 2027: Okorocha ‘never contested’ Imo West primary – Uzodimma’s aide
item.description: By Omeiza Ajayi – ABUJA The Deputy Chief of Staff to Imo State Governor, Senator Hope Uzodimma, Chief Enyinna Onuegbu, has said former Governor Rochas Okorocha never took part in the All Progressives Congress APC primary for Imo West Senatorial District, which a Federal High Court in Abuja has now ruled he won. Read Also: Orlu Senatorial Seat: War in Imo as Okorocha battles Uzodimma Onuegbu, a lawyer, spoke on Friday evening on Arise News, monitored in Abuja, in a right of reply to Okorocha, who appeared on the same programme about 24 hours earlier. “Imo APC people never saw Okorocha as an aspirant and he didn’t participate and was not even physically present in Imo State anywhere at any level. Any briefing of stakeholders, any briefing of delegates, any event conducted prior to that primaries, Senator Okorocha was not physically present,” Onuegbu sai He asked at what stage Okorocha addressed party members as an aspirant. “At what stage did he consult? At what stage has he been able to provide evidence of I have been declared winner at any level, ward, LGA or state?” he asked. Onuegbu said the Independent National Electoral Commission (INEC) and the committee that conducted the primary both rejected the documents Okorocha relied on before the court. “When the court, in its own documentation, the processes filed in court, showed that both INEC, the authority that supervised, APC committee that conducted, all denied the documents His Excellency Rochas Okorocha relied on. Before the court, they all denied them as forgeries, fictitious, and totally fabricated,” he said. According to him, the court “chose to rely on what applicant filed without averting its mind to the need to resolve the conflict in the documentation brought by both parties.” Onuegbu argued that where documents conflict in an originating summons, “the law requires the court to resolve the conflict by oral evidence of witnesses.” In his words, “What the law requires the court to do is to call evidence of witnesses so that they can be put to cross-examination.” He added that the Supreme Court had held that “when forgeries are alleged, what the court is left to do is to put the parties to the witness box.” Asked whether Uzodimma’s side had been denied the chance to present its own documents, Onuegbu said that was not the point. “He put forward documents and we put documents that showed that the authority that did the work disputed what he put. So this contradiction can only be resolved” by hearing witnesses, he said. He rejected Okorocha’s reference to “Hope’s document,” saying the governor did not run the exercise. “Governor Hope Uzodimma was not the one who conducted the primaries. He was an aspirant like he was. Governor Hope Uzodimma was not the person who declared the result,” he said. item.title: Masussuka: Life, preaching, death
item.description: The murder of Katsina-based Islamic cleric, Sheikh Yahaya Ibrahim Masussuka, has stirred emotions and sparked conversations around the life and times of a popular preacher seen through different lenses. To his army of followers, he embodied peace, dignity and tolerance for religious differences. To his critics, he was a controversial scholar whose religious ideology and preaching were questionable. Masussuka was shot dead alongside his associate, Adamu Abubakar, on Monday evening in front of his house at Dutsin-Ma, Katsina State, in an attack claimed by the extremist group, Ansaru. Amnesty International has called on the Nigerian government to conduct a thorough investigation into the killing and ensure that those responsible are brought to justice. Masussuka: We reject his ideology but condemn his killing – JIBWIS Imam Masussuka’s preaching, killing contrary to Islamic laws – Sheikh Maraya The 47-year-old cleric subscribed to and preached Quranic teachings, but, to greater extent, disregarded Hadith, the sayings and practices of Prophet Muhammad (PBUH) – a stance that placed him at variance with his critics. He alleged that a lot of Hadiths being attributed to the Prophet were not from him, saying they were concocted by some people out of mischief. Masussuka reportedly began preaching at the tender age of 13 and rose to prominence with the advent of social media, through which he established himself as one of the most vocal clerics among the Qur’aniyun Islamic sect. Through his active social media platforms, his preaching gained more recognition, increasingly attracting attention from other sects with different ideologies. Masussuka’s increased visibility drew controversies around his ideology. One major controversy surrounding Masussuka’s teachings and ideology revolved around his rejection of certain Hadith traditions as authorities and forms of religious practice. According to other sects, his doctrine that only the Qur’an serves as the gateway to religious practice goes contrary to a larger belief that both the Qur’an and the Sunnah of the Prophet are central sources of Islamic guidance. Disagreements over his ideology became more pronounced and his teachings were challenged on several occasions. Though disagreement on the interpretation and authority of Hadith has long existed among Muslim scholars, Masussuka’s unique stance on the matter placed him at odds with scholars who considered his teachings inconsistent with established Islamic traditions. Amid growing scrutiny of his preaching, the Katsina State Government, on November 18, 2025, announced that Masussuka would be required to defend his teachings before a committee of Islamic scholars established based on the several calls. The meeting, however, didn’t see the light of day due to undisclosed circumstances, as he continued to challenge other sects that go against his ideologies. item.title: Parallel campaigns within APC
item.description: While the All Progressives Congress (APC) officially kicked off its presidential campaign last week, a major hindrance to its effective spread in all the geopolitical zones and states in the country has remained the lack of synergy in many states. Weekend Trust checks revealed that there are many states where leaders of the party claiming to work for the reelection of its presidential candidate, President Bola Ahmed Tinubu, prefer to work in isolated camps, without as much as involving other leaders in its operations. This, our correspondent learnt, is due to unresolved leadership disputes, personality clashes and the bid outdo each other to prove the one with the bigger political worth. The intensity, however, varies in degree from state to state, with some openly defying each other, while some put up a façade of working together, but beneath the surface are trying to undermine each other’s efforts. Masussuka: Life, preaching, death Nigeria’s drug battle Investigations reveal that in states where the governors joined the APC only after winning elections, the process of integrating the party structure on ground has not been concluded, leading to suspicion between those who moved the governors and those they met on ground. In states like Plateau, Taraba, Adamawa and Kano, there are still vestiges of animosity between the two major camps of the defecting governors and those they met on ground. In states like Anambra and Osun, where the governors are members of other parties but have been integrated into the APC presidential campaign council, the preexisting party structures there have shown that they are not comfortable with the arrangement. States like Benue, Ondo, Katsina, Zamfara have shown that the contending forces are not aligned to work together for the reelection bid of its presidential candidate due to unrestrained rivalries between the governors and other powerful figures from the party in their states, who have the ears of Abuja. Our correspondents capture what is going on in some of the states. Masari yet to attend Radda’s campaign rallies in Katsina As the Katsina State chapter of the All Progressives Congress (APC) begins its 2027 re-election campaign, the Special Adviser to President Bola Ahmed Tinubu on Political and Other Matters, Alhaji Ibrahim Kabir Masari, is yet to attend any of the party’s major campaign activities in the state. Masari, who is considered one of the influential APC figures in Katsina, was absent during the inauguration of the Dikko/Tinubu Campaign Council by Governor Dikko Umaru Radda. He was also missing at the official flag-off of the campaign in Funtua Local Government Area. However, rather than joining the governor at the public campaign events, Masari is said to have intensified separate political consultations within and outside Katsina State ahead of the 2027 general elections. item.title: Nigeria’s drug battle
item.description: Despite massive seizures, arrest of Nigerians and foreign nationals, prosecution and dismantling of clandestine methamphetamine laboratories linked to international criminal networks by the National Drug Law Enforcement Agency (NDLEA), among others, drug trafficking remains a major challenge in Nigeria. From industrial-scale drug production to cocaine couriers and cross-border syndicates, the persistence of the illicit trade raises questions about the sophistication of criminal networks and the factors sustaining the business. The growing drug problem has continued to impact negatively on the health and general wellbeing of many Nigerians, especially the youth population. Many families and households note that they are going through a lot of trauma and pains in the management and rehabilitation of their children and loved ones who have become victims of drug addiction. Masussuka: Life, preaching, death Parallel campaigns within APC According to data from the NDLEA, over the last five years, a total of 96,157 suspects, including 250 drug barons, have been arrested; 15, 833, 856.3kgs of illicit drug seized with 2,099.96 hectares of cannabis farms destroyed. Within the same period, the agency secured 18,691 convictions while 54, 517 were counselled and rehabilitated. Between January 2026 and September 2026 alone, data showed that 18,290 arrests have been made with illicit drug seizures of 698,488.76kgs while 81.69 hectares of cannabis farms have been destroyed across the country. Within the same period, a total of 2,568 convictions were recorded while 5,681 were counselled and rehabilitated. The agency has also recorded the dismantling of four industrial meth laboratories across four states in recent months. Besides the destructions of meth laboratories, international drug traffickers, including those from South Africa and other parts of the world, have also been arrested in recent months, with some already facing prosecution. The agency also announced drug recoveries across several states, including Lagos, Kano, Bauchi, Niger, Edo, Ondo, Taraba, Oyo and Delta, anong others. Notwithstanding the massive seizures, arrests, convictions and destruction of illicit drugs by the agency, the drug trafficking challenge remains potent, with experts saying that Nigeria is not just a transit route for illicit drug but also evolving as a production hub. In this report, Weekend Trust examines some of the factors making Nigeria a drug trafficking destination and production hub, impacts on drug users and abusers, nexus between drug trafficking and insecurity, and the way forward. item.title: Orlu Senatorial Seat: War in Imo as Okorocha battles Uzodimma
item.description: •Court grants Okorocha ticket, 12 Chairmen back go vernor By Omeiza Ajayi – ABUJA The fight over who flies the All Progressives Congress (APC) flag in Imo West Senatorial District has turned into open war, with the party’s 12 local government chairmen in the zone rejecting a court judgment that handed the ticket to former Governor Rochas Okorocha and insisting that Governor Hope Uzodimma remains the candidate. Read Also: Tinubu has broken Imo’s shackles — Okorocha hails court judgment The chairmen made their stand known on Friday at a press conference in Owerri, a day after a Federal High Court in Abuja sacked Uzodimma as the party’s candidate for the January 16, 2027 Senate election. State APC chairman, Austin Onyedebelu spoke on behalf of the Chairmen. Said he: “We reject this judgment in its entirety because it is an undisguised travesty of justice. It is a political robbery clothed in legal robes, the latest instalment of a satanic scheme hatched by Abuja politicians against the South-East,” the chairmen declared. Justice Obiora Egwuatu ruled on Thursday that Okorocha, and not the governor, won the party’s May 18 primary for the district. He held that Okorocha had produced “sufficient evidence” that he won the exercise, which was monitored by the Independent National Electoral Commission (INEC). Court order The court ordered the APC to forward Okorocha’s name to INEC and directed the commission to publish him as the party’s validly nominated candidate. It also barred Uzodimma from presenting himself as the APC candidate in the election. The chairmen said they were in the field on May 18, 2026, when the primary was held, and that Okorocha scored only 1,098 votes against about 230,000 for Uzodimma, who was declared winner in the presence of INEC staff. “For the avoidance of doubt, we NEVER VOTED FOR ROCHAS OKOROCHA,” Onyedebelu said. “This legal somersault orchestrated by enemies of Ndigbo was obviously procured not only to destabilise Orlu zone but to consolidate the war of attrition by some Nigerians to politically hold down the south east.” They said Okorocha never used the window provided by the party to petition its appeal panel over any irregularity, only to go to court and be handed victory. The chairmen pointed to what they called wild celebrations by Okorocha since Thursday and his remarks that he got help from higher quarters outside the court. In their view, this showed a conspiracy to shut Ndigbo out of political relevance. They said they were enraged that people outside Igboland wanted to use Okorocha as an errand boy to supplant the wish of the majority of APC members in the Orlu zone, who overwhelmingly voted for Uzodimma. “Our grievance lies with a small circle of power brokers who appear determined that no Igbo man shall come close to the first, second, or third positions in the land. We therefore appeal to President Bola Ahmed Tinubu, whose leadership we support and will continue to support, to look closely at the men behind t

item.title: ‘Northern leaders begged Tinubu to support Buhari, promised to return power after eight years’ – APC chieftain
item.description: By Muhammad Inuwa, Dutse ‎ ‎A chieftain of the All Progressives Congress, APC, and former House of Representative member representing Birnin-Kudu/ Buji in Jigawa State, Engr. Magaji Da’u Aliyu, has claimed that Northern political leaders begged President Bola Tinubu to support former President Muhammadu Buhari’s presidential ambition and promised to return power to his side after eight years. ‎Aliyu, who is also the Deputy Campaign Director of the North for Tinubu Support Group, disclosed this while addressing supporters in Birnin Kudu. ‎He said the North has no justification for opposing Tinubu’s re-election in the 2027 general election, insisting that the region must honour the political agreement allegedly reached before Buhari became president in 2015. ‎ ‎According to him, Buhari had contested the presidential election three times without success before Northern political leaders approached Tinubu in Lagos to seek his support. ‎ ‎”Buhari contested the presidential election three times and lost. We then went to Lagos to beg Tinubu to support Buhari’s presidential ambition,” he said. ‎ ‎”He agreed to support us on the understanding that after Buhari’s eight years in office, power would return to his side, and we accepted the agreement.” ‎ ‎Aliyu maintained that supporting Tinubu’s re-election in 2027 is a matter of honouring the promise made to him, stressing that Northerners have no reason to abandon the agreement. ‎ ‎”For every Northerner, fulfilling that agreement is mandatory. We have no reason not to honour the agreement we entered into,” he said. ‎ ‎The APC chieftain pledged that members of the Northern Tinubu Support Group would commit their resources towards ensuring the President’s victory in the next presidential election. ‎ ‎”On our part, we will support Tinubu’s re-election bid with our lives and wealth to ensure that we fulfil the promise we made,” he added. ‎ ‎Speaking on insecurity, Aliyu also defended President Tinubu against criticism over the country’s security challenges. ‎ ‎He argued that no human being has absolute power to guarantee security, insisting that only God can provide lasting peace and stability. ‎ ‎”Let us stop the blame game. Only God has the power to provide security. We should seek His forgiveness, and He will grant us peace and stability,” he said. item.title: Happy Halloween! SpaceX launches 27 Starlink satellites to orbit from California
item.description: null SpaceX celebrated Halloween with an early-morning launch from California. A Falcon 9 rocket lifted off from Vandenberg Space Force Base today (Oct. 31) at 12:04 a.m. EDT (0404 GMT; 9:04 p.m. on Oct. 30 local time), sending 27 of the company's Starlink internet satellites to low Earth orbit (LEO). The Falcon 9's first stage came back to Earth as planned, touching down about 8.5 minutes after launch on the SpaceX drone ship "Of Course I Still Love You," which was stationed in the Pacific Ocean. The Falcon 9's first stage rests on the deck of a drone ship shortly after launch on Oct. 31, 2026. (Image credit: SpaceX) It was the 18th flight for this particular booster, which is designated B1093. The record for a SpaceX first stage is 37 , set this past August by the booster B1067. The Falcon 9's upper stage did its job as well today, deploying the 27 Starlink satellites into LEO about 62 minutes after launch. They're joining more than 11,000 spacecraft in the Starlink megaconstellation, which is by far the largest satellite network ever assembled. Previous Booster 1093 launches SDA-T1TL-B | SDA-T1TL-C | Transporter-16 | 14 Starlink missions Today's launch was the 118th Falcon 9 flight of 2026 so far. More than 70% of these missions have been devoted to building out the Starlink network. SpaceX has also launched its Falcon Heavy and Starship rockets three times apiece this year. Falcon Heavy is an operational vehicle, but Starship remains in the test-flight phase. The company is currently gearing up for another Starship launch , which is expected to take place sometime in November.

item.title: ‘Debt worse than leprosy’ – Obasanjo tackles Tinubu
item.description: By James Ogunnaike, Abeokuta Former President Olusegun Obasanjo has criticised President Bola Tinubu’s defence of government borrowing, declaring that debt is worse than leprosy because of its devastating consequences for present and future generations. Obasanjo also warned Nigeria and other African countries against allowing foreign interests to dominate artificial intelligence, AI, saying the emerging technology could become another instrument of exploitation and digital colonialism if the continent failed to develop its own technological capacity. The former president spoke on Friday in Abeokuta, Ogun State, at the Ajibosin Platform, a public forum themed, “Leveraging Artificial Intelligence to Solve Grassroots Problems and Accelerate National Development”. Reacting to Tinubu’s earlier assertion that borrowing was not leprosy, Obasanjo argued that the accumulation of public debt could mortgage the country’s future and impose an unbearable burden on generations yet unborn. “And for anybody to say debt is no leprosy, is absolute nonsense. Debt is worse than leprosy because leprosy destroys only one person. Debt destroys generations,” he declared. Tinubu had defended his administration’s borrowing policy in April, insisting that borrowing was not inherently wrong if the country had the capacity to repay. “If we have to borrow, we borrow. Borrowing is not leprosy; we just have to work hard to be able to pay for it,” the President had said during a meeting with Plateau State leaders, led by Governor Caleb Mutfwang and the National Chairman of the All Progressives Congress, Prof. Nentawe Yilwatda, at the State House. The President’s position came amid concerns over Nigeria’s rising debt profile and the increasing proportion of government revenue committed to debt servicing. Obasanjo also questioned Nigeria’s economic performance over the years, particularly the depreciation of the naira against the United States dollar. Recounting his experience as a farmer, he said the naira was stronger than the dollar when he established his farm 47 years ago. “When I started my farm, 47 years ago, naira to the dollar was one naira to $1.85. Forty-seven years ago. What has Nigeria done in 47 years that we now have 1,500 naira to a dollar? What have we done?” he asked. He challenged the country’s political leadership to demonstrate its understanding of Nigeria’s problems and identify practical solutions to the challenges confronting the nation. “What do our leaders know? And what do they not know? And from what they know, what can they do for us?” he queried. The former president also faulted Nigeria’s dependence on the World Bank and International Monetary Fund (IMF), arguing that their economic prescriptions were not necessarily designed to address the country’s peculiar circumstances. “World Bank and IMF were not designed for us. They were not built by us. They were built before we became independent. And that’s the people who would determine what we do,” he sa

item.title: Drunk barber allegedly stabs man to death in Jigawa
item.description: By Muhammad Inuwa, Dutse The Jigawa State Police Command has arrested a 29-year-old barber, Emmanuel Olatonok, for allegedly stabbing a 32-year-old man, Ibrahim Shago, to death while reportedly under the influence of alcohol. The Police Public Relations Officer, SP Shiisu Lawan Adam, disclosed this in a statement issued to journalists. The incident occurred on Thursday, October 29, 2026, at about 5:45 p.m. in the Rafin Sanyi area of Dutse Local Government Area. According to the police spokesperson, the suspect, who reportedly worked as a barber at a hotel in Dutse, allegedly stabbed the victim in the neck with a knife following an argument. He added that the suspect was allegedly under the influence of alcohol at the time of the incident. “The suspect, a barber reportedly working at a popular hotel in Dutse, allegedly stabbed the victim in the neck with a knife following an argument,” he said. Adam explained that the victim, a resident of Karnaya town, was immediately rushed to a hospital for medical attention but was later confirmed dead by a medical doctor. He said the incident triggered tension in the area as some angry youths gathered at the scene and attempted to vandalise the hotel. However, police operatives from Dutse Division quickly intervened and brought the situation under control, preventing further violence and destruction of property. The police spokesperson confirmed that the suspect is currently in custody, while investigations are ongoing to establish the circumstances surrounding the killing. He added that the suspect would be charged to court upon the conclusion of the investigation. item.title: 21 cars affected as fire engulfs Lagos mechanic workshop
item.description: By Evelyn Usman A mechanic workshop went up in flames in the early hours of yesterday at Isheri-Idimu, Alimosho Local Government Area of Lagos State, with 21 vehicles reportedly affected. The fire, which broke out at about 3:05am on Oladunni Street, beside Eternal Filling Station, reportedly threatened to spread to the adjoining petrol station, raising fears of a possible major disaster, according to eyewitnesses. However, the swift intervention of emergency responders reportedly prevented the inferno from spreading to the filling station and nearby buildings. The Lagos State Emergency Management Agency (LASEMA) said its Dolphin Response Team, stationed at Igando, was immediately activated following a distress call. The Permanent Secretary of LASEMA, Dr Olufemi Oke-Osanyintolu, said: “Upon arrival, responders discovered that the fire had engulfed a mechanical workshop where several exotic vehicles were parked, in close proximity to a petroleum filling station. Through the prompt, professional and coordinated intervention of the LASEMA Response Team and the Lagos State Fire and Rescue Service, supported by the Lagos Neighbourhood Safety Corps and the Nigeria Police Force, the inferno was prevented from spreading to the filling station and surrounding structures, thereby averting what could have been a major disaster. “The fire has been completely extinguished and damping-down operations concluded. Preliminary assessment indicates that about twenty-one (21) exotic vehicles were affected, with a section of a nearby building sustaining minor damage. “Importantly, no loss of life and no injury were recorded. “The Lagos State Government, through LASEMA, reiterates its commitment to the protection of lives and property across the state. The agency commends the bravery and diligence of all responders whose swift action ensured that the incident was brought under control without casualties. “Members of the public are enjoined to continue to prioritise safety measures, particularly in workshops and environments where inflammable materials are handled, and to promptly alert emergency services through the toll-free emergency numbers 767 and 112 in the event of any emergency,” he said. item.title: Can Tinubu’s education reforms rescue a generation? – Inside Alausa’s ambitious agenda
item.description: By Joseph Erunke, Abuja With nearly 46 million children reportedly captured in a new education data system, almost 250,000 Nigerians undergoing technical skills training and the government claiming to have returned one million out-of-school children to classrooms, the Tinubu administration is making an ambitious case for an education turnaround. But can impressive figures translate into lasting educational transformation? For decades, Nigeria’s education crisis has been defined by millions of children outside classrooms, overcrowded schools, inadequate facilities, poorly equipped laboratories, frustrated teachers and graduates struggling to find employment despite their qualifications Now, in the office of the Minister of Education, Dr Tunji Alausa, a digital dashboard is offering a different picture–one the minister says provides an unprecedented opportunity to monitor schools, track enrolment, identify infrastructure gaps and examine the distribution of teachers and pupils nationwide. With a few clicks, Alausa explained, officials can drill down into individual schools to examine enrollment figures, the number of girls, available facilities and teaching personnel. For a country long challenged by fragmented education statistics, this represents a potentially significant shift. But the real test of Nigeria’s education reforms is not how impressive the dashboard appears in Abuja. It is whether the technology delivers better classrooms, competent teachers, improved learning outcomes and greater opportunities for millions of children. That is the central question confronting Alausa as he presents President Bola Tinubu’s education reforms as the beginning of a measurable turnaround. Alausa Speaking while receiving notification of his selection for Vanguard’s Public Sector Icon of the Year award, the minister outlined six priority areas: technical and vocational education and training, science and technology education, reducing the out-of-school population, girls’ education, data and digitalisation, and improving educational quality and teacher effectiveness. Together, these priorities seek to address a fundamental contradiction in Nigerian education: expanding access without guaranteeing learning, producing graduates without adequate practical skills and increasing enrolment without providing sufficient infrastructure. With Nigeria’s population estimated at approximately 220 million and a youthful demographic, Alausa argued that education reform was imperative. The challenge is to turn this demographic advantage into economic productivity rather than allow it to deepen unemployment, inequality and insecurity Perhaps the most consequential element of Alausa’s presentation was the ministry’s cloud-based education dashboard, which he said captures information on nearly 46 million children. Its potential lies in replacing fragmented administrative records with a more comprehensive picture of the education system. Reliable information could help authorit

item.title: APOD: 2026 October 31 – Night on a Spooky Planet
item.description: APOD Science APOD APOD: 2026 October 31 –… Today’s APOD Archive Submissions Index Search Calendar RSS Education About Discuss APOD Astronomy Picture of the Day Discover the cosmos! Each day a different image or photograph of our fascinating universe is featured, along with a brief explanation written by a professional astronomer. Night on a Spooky Planet Explanation: What spooky planet is this? Planet Earth on a dark and stormy night, of course. The ghostly scene was photographed at Hverir , a geothermally active area found along northeastern Iceland’s volcanic landscape . Triggered by solar activity , geomagnetic storms have unleashed energetic particles trapped in Earth’s magnetic field. Penetrating the planet’s upper atmosphere at high latitudes, the particles create auroral displays in the starry night sky. Ghostly towers of steam and gas are venting from local fumaroles to dance against the eerie, greenish northern lights. For now, auroral activity on planet Earth remains in a high state as the Sun is only in early phases of decline from the peak of its solar activity cycle . And soon, other ghostly apparitions may dance in your neighborhood. Happy Halloween ! item.title: Once again, NASA is asking for ideas to rescue Hubble from certain death
item.description: The Hubble Space Telescope still shines in the eyes of astronomers after 36 years in orbit, but it is not as nimble as it once was. Left alone, the observatory will plunge back into the atmosphere in the early-to-mid-2030s, closing the book on one of the most famous scientific instruments of the century. NASA last raised the orbit of Hubble in 2002, when the Space Shuttle Columbia visited the observatory for a servicing mission. The final shuttle servicing flight in 2009 did not reboost the telescope's orbit, and with the retirement of the shuttle fleet two years later, Hubble has steadily lost altitude with no way to stave off eventual destruction. The space agency released a Request For Information (RFI) on Thursday asking commercial companies for ideas on how to reboost, service, or a controlled disposal of Hubble. Responses are due November 30. Specifically, NASA is looking for information about companies' current and near-term capabilities for capturing Hubble and boosting it to an altitude of at least 373 miles (600 km), enhancing the telescope's performance, or guiding Hubble to a controlled reentry. item.title: The world mourns the passing of 'Star Trek's' Patrick Stewart with a galaxy of tearful tributes
item.description: null As we all begin to absorb the bitter news of Patrick Stewart's death at the age of 86, a flood of personal tributes are pouring in, reflecting this global treasure's wonderful life lived with a dignity and bravado that few mortals possess. We’re getting just a hint of what Patrick Stewart meant to those who worked with him or knew him throughout his stellar career. Whether on stage with the Royal Shakespeare Company, on TV as the dashing Captain Jean-Luc Picard in " Star Trek: The Next Generation ," and in Hollywood spectacles like 1984's "Dune," four " Star Trek " feature films, and the many "X-Men" movies in which he portrayed Professor Charles Xavier, Stewart was always the consummate professional. His final screen performance arrives on Dec. 18 with "Avengers: Doomsday" where he’ll present his Charles Xavier character once more. "Before everything else, Patrick was defined by being born and bred in Yorkshire, the proud county in the north of England which he loved to the end," Ian McKellen wrote on Instagram of his "X-Men" co-star and friend. "You could hear it in his accented voice and in the stern honesty with which he told you what he thought and felt. Yorkshiremen have no truck with half-truths or avoidance of big issues. He wore his heart on his sleeve, which made him a man to rely on, to admire and, in my case, love." Patrick Stewart and Ian McKellan in 2000's "X-Men." (Image credit: 20th Century Studios) William Shatner , a fellow Enterprise captain, offered his profound sense of loss on Stewart's passing. The legends shared the screen in 1994's "Star Trek: Generations." "What a heartbreaking week it has been. Sir Patrick Stewart was a friend, a colleague, and a magnificent actor," Shatner posted on Facebook . "From the stage to the bridge of the Enterprise, he brought intelligence, grace, and a deep sense of humanity to everything he did. Captain Picard stood for the best of us, and so did the man who played him. I was filled with affection and admiration for him and his work. My heart goes out to Sunny and his family. He will be deeply missed." Patrick Stewart and William Shatner star in 1994's "Star Trek: Generations." (Image credit: Paramount) Akiva Goldsman, co-creator of Paramount+'s " Star Trek: Picard " and "Star Trek: Strange New Worlds," delivered a sorrowful message in the aftermath of Stewart's death "Patrick was not only a true lion of the profession, he was the rarest of alchemists, one who could literally turn the written word into flesh and blood," Goldsman wrote. "Patrick was kind, strong, fiercely intelligent, collaborative, vulnerable and wise. His Captain Jean-Luc Picard permanently expanded the universe of 'Star Trek' without measure. He will be deeply missed by this one fan and by so many more." Stewart's "Star Trek: The Next Generation" family shared their grief and offered up poignant words to try to describe what effect he had on their lives and profession. item.title: Flesh-eating screwworms spread to third state and are attacking pets
item.description: For a genuine fright this Halloween, you can turn your gaze to the southern border, where ravenous, flesh-eating maggots are festering and have taken to eating people's pets. This week, the country's New World Screwworm (NWS) infestation spread to a third state, Arizona, which joins New Mexico and Texas in being plagued by the horrifying parasites. To date, 74 animal cases have been identified in the US since the flies re-invaded the country in June. The flies lay hundreds of eggs in wounds and moist orifices of animals, and the resulting voracious maggots feast on their victims. The maggots resemble screws and tortuously bore and twist into living flesh, causing severe, sometimes fatal wounds, before dropping to the ground to develop into adults. Read full article Comments

item.title: Oh captain, our captain: Ars staff remembers Patrick Stewart
item.description: Along with the rest of the world, we at Ars are mourning Sir Patrick Stewart —the beloved award-winning actor best known as Captain Jean-Luc Picard in Star Trek: The Next Generation and Professor Charles Xavier in the X-Men franchise—who died yesterday at the age of 86. A statement released by Stewart's representatives said: We announce with great sorrow the passing of Sir Patrick Stewart yesterday at his home in Los Angeles, in the loving care of his beloved wife Sunny, following a brief and poignant journey with Alzheimer’s Disease and Lewy Body Dementia. He has been held in the warm embrace of family and friends, surrounded by live music, prayer, tears, laughter, and the kind of profound emotion that only he could inspire after a lifetime of devotion to us all. We will forever cherish the peaceful ease and reflection on his face, an enduring reminder of his invincible grace. Through the actor's X account , the family has requested that, in lieu of flowers, memorial contributions be made to the Johns Hopkins Alzheimer’s Disease Research Center Fund and the Alzheimer’s Foundation of America Caregiver Resources . item.title: Anthropic VS code extension on Cursor backdoored for nearly 12 hours
item.description: An official extension for Anthropic’s Claude model was backdoored and threatened as many as 5,000 developers' machines, multiple sources reported Friday. Anthropic so far has yet to warn customers of the incident. The compromised package was a VS Code extension available in the marketplace of Cursor, a maker of AI-assisted developer tools, the company said Friday. The malicious version, 2.1.313, subsequently affected “at most 5,000 users,” presumably when they either downloaded it or their systems automatically fetched and installed it. Anthropic pushed version 2.1.314 several hours after the previous version became available on Cursor, according to independent researcher Kevin Beaumont. Both Beaumont and the CTO and co-founder of security firm Phorian said that version 2.1.313 was distributed through Anthropic’s official account on Cursor. So far, neither Cursor nor Anthropic has explained how the attackers gained control of the account. In search of cloud credentials “It was a supply-chain compromise where the attacker gained access to the official distribution channel,” Phorian CTO and co-founder Luke Roberts told Ars. “The malicious version 2.1.313 was posted to the official Anthropic account, effectively superseding 2.1.312. Extensions auto-update in Cursor by default, but users can configure this in settings.” Phorian has more details here . Read full article Comments

item.title: An aquanaut comes home: Returning to Earth from an undersea 'space station'
item.description:
Dr. Michaela Musilova is an award-winning astrobiologist, explorer, professional speaker and author. Michaela has been conducting space-related research at institutions around the world, including NASA, ESA, CalTech, the Canada-France-Hawaii telescope and many others. She was the Commander of 40 simulated missions to the Moon and Mars — the most missions led to date.

Currently, Michaela is the President and Founder of the nonprofit XtremeFrontiers. She is pioneering a unique global project: Astro Seven Summits. It's a world-first in combining expeditions to the highest mountain on each continent with scientific research in collaboration with NASA and institutions worldwide, educational activities and filming documentaries.

Michaela is also a consultant for numerous companies across the globe for topics ranging from Mars missions all the way to museum exhibitions, such as for the Smithsonian. She is one of very few people to have ever led research projects on all seven continents.

Michaela’s work has been recognized through numerous awards, such as Forbes 30 Under 30, Top 100 Women in Aerospace and Aviation, and the Emerging Space Leaders Grant.

Michaela is regularly invited to give keynote presentations and performs a variety of outreach activities globally as a science communicator. She has been giving interviews to international media for over 20 years, writing scientific and educational articles, and she co-authored her biography, "Woman from Mars."

Our time on our "space mission" underwater was coming to an end, and I felt like what I imagine an astronaut on the International Space Station (ISS) must feel before returning to Earth. On one hand, you are excited to return to your home and loved ones, as well as to fresh food and normal hygiene. On the other, you know you will miss your crew and the incredible experience of being in space. While my SEA STAR crew and I had not left Earth during our mission, we were separated from the surface of our home planet for five days. All we saw was a green alien water world surrounding us. We did this to live and work like astronauts on the ISS . Instead of dealing with the challenges of space that astronauts face, we problem-solved sometimes equally difficult issues that divers have to manage when performing research in sea water. Our "wet ISS" was the Jules' Undersea Lab, which is located near Key Largo, Florida, at 22 feet (7 meters) underwater. By the end of our mission, we had all officially become aquanauts. An aquanaut is an undersea explorer who remains underwater for more than 24 hours, without returning to the surface, in a state known as saturation. Paul Bakken conducting equipment testing. item.title: Debt Worse Than Leprosy, Destroys Generations, Says Obasanjo
item.description: Former President Olusegun Obasanjo has criticised President Bola Tinubu over his position on borrowing, declaring that debt is worse than leprosy because it destroys generations. He stated this while speaking at a symposium, a public forum focused on leveraging Artificial Intelligence to solve grassroots problems and accelerate national development in Abeokuta, Ogun State. Tinubu had said in April that borrowing should not be viewed negatively, insisting that the government would borrow when necessary, provided it could repay the loans. President Bola Tinubu (Photo: X@aonanuga1956) But Obasanjo disagreed, describing such a position as absolute nonsense. The former president also questioned Nigeria’s economic performance, recalling that when he established his farm 47 years ago, the naira exchanged at ₦1 to $1 and 85 cents. He challenged the country’s leadership to explain the naira’s depreciation to about ₦1,500 to a dollar, questioning what Nigeria had achieved over the decades. Meanwhile, the guest speaker, historian and public policy scholar, Umar Ardo, has warned that artificial intelligence could deepen Africa’s dependence on foreign powers if the continent fails to control its technology and digital infrastructure. Ardo warned that without investments in chip fabrication, data centres, African-owned datasets and continental cooperation, artificial intelligence could become another tool for managing Africa rather than empowering the continent to determine its own future. Amid criticism, President Tinubu on Thursday defended his administration’s plan to take more foreign loans , arguing that Nigeria needs long-term investment in infrastructure to achieve its ambition of becoming a $1 trillion economy by 2030. The President said the proposed loans would be used to build roads, improve electricity supply, upgrade ports and fund other projects that would create jobs, grow businesses and provide opportunities for future generations. In a statement titled “From Reforms to Delivery: Our Infrastructure Investment and Growth Strategy,” Tinubu said the focus should be on what the borrowed money would achieve rather than how much the government was borrowing. “The key question is not how much we borrow, but what we build, the value we create and the future we leave behind,” he said. He listed the Lagos-Calabar Coastal Highway, Sokoto-Badagry Superhighway, Trans-Sahara Superhighway, electricity grid improvements and upgrades to major commercial ports in Lagos among the projects the government plans to fund. He said the projects, alongside investments in healthcare, education and vocational training, would connect economic regions, reduce the cost of transporting goods, support farming and industries, and attract private investors. The President said the Lagos-Calabar Coastal Highway alone could reduce transport costs along its route by 15 to 20 per cent and add up to two per cent to Nigeria’s Gross Domestic Product (GDP) through increased trade, tourism

This week, Schnell discovered the depths of the problem himself as he resigned from the university after an advisory committee found that he failed to disclose significant AI use in an academic paper and in the Washington Post op-ed, even though publishers required such disclosure. Schnell didn't make it especially easy for the committee to investigate his AI use; the report uses the term "insufficient cooperation." He did turn over his Dartmouth laptop, but he did not turn over logs from his personal LLM accounts related to the writings in question. Nor did he agree to meet with the committee. The committee did get access to the Claude enterprise account Schnell had used through Dartmouth, though. This shows him using the LLM as a tool for revising his papers, finding and fixing bugs in code, and editing or generating figures. item.title: Fani-Kayode Presents Letters Of Credence, Assumes Duties As High Commissioner In South Africa
item.description: A former Minister of Aviation, Femi Fani-Kayode, has formally presented copies of his Letters of Credence to the Deputy Director-General, Public Diplomacy, and Acting Chief of State Protocol, Mr Clayson Monyela, at the South African Department of International Relations and Cooperation (DIRCO). The presentation on Friday marked an important diplomatic milestone, signifying the formal commencement of Fani-Kayode’s diplomatic functions and his assumption of duties as Nigeria’s High Commissioner to South Africa with effect from October 30, 2026. This photo shows Nigeria’s High Commissioner to South Africa, Femi Fani-Kayode (centre), meeting with South African officials on October 30, 2026. Following the presentation, Fani-Kayode also met with the Deputy Director-General of DIRCO in his office, as part of his initial diplomatic engagements with senior South African government officials. The presentation of copies of his Letters of Credence precedes the ceremonial presentation of his Letters of Credence to South Africa’s President Cyril Ramaphosa, which will take place in a few days. This photo shows Nigeria’s High Commissioner to South Africa, Femi Fani-Kayode (left), presenting his Letters of Credence on October 30, 2026. In a statement dated October 28, the Department of International Relations and Cooperation of the Republic of South Africa explained that the Minister of International Relations and Cooperation had approved a policy change in terms of Article 13 (1) of the Vienna Convention on Diplomatic Relations, 1961, to replace the current practice where a Head of Mission-Designate would have to present the original Letters of Credence to the President before being considered as having taken up their functions in the receiving state. “The Department wishes to confirm that once the Head of Mission-Designate has submitted the copies of the Letters of Credence to the Chief of State Protocol, the said Head of Mission-Designate is considered to have taken up his / her position as Head of Mission,” the statement read in part. “The Department wishes to furthermore confirm that the original Letters of Credence will still be handed over to the President at the next Credentials Ceremony on a date and time to be communicated. The Department of International Relations and Cooperation of the Republic of South Africa avails itself of this opportunity to renew to the High Commission of the Federal Republic of Nigeria the assurances of its highest consideration.” The post Fani-Kayode Presents Letters Of Credence, Assumes Duties As High Commissioner In South Africa appeared first on Channels Television .

item.title: Darkbloom, which allowed Mac users to rent out their GPUs for AI inference, warns of low payouts
item.description: Declining token prices have prompted Darkbloom, a distributed inference network, to reassess its business plans. Darkbloom , a project from Seattle-based tech biz Eigen Labs, has developed software that allows anyone with a sufficiently capable macOS device to rent their GPU through the Darkbloom network for interference jobs. In return, they get paid. Through this network, 800 or so participants – including as of two days ago this reporter – have been able to collect a few cents to a few dollars per day by having their hardware handle AI model prompts submitted through OpenRouter , an AI model gateway. In theory, someone running one of Apple's recently released Mac minis with an M5 Pro chip and 64 GB of RAM could earn as much as $192 per month handling incoming inference jobs, per the company's estimate. That assumes full 24/7 utilization during this period on a sought-after model like Qwen3.6 35B A3B, which sells for $0.065/M input tokens, $0.75/M output tokens. But not every network participant has fully surrendered their Mac hardware to the network. The median earnings of the 50 people on the leaderboard amount to about $5.26 per day, $159.86 per month, or $1,918.50 per year. So the best case estimate presented by Darkbloom looks plausible. But it may not be sustainable. The price of tokens – the unit of AI work – has declined, reportedly down 54 percent since May . Ramp's AI Token Price Index , which tracks the price of tokens from Anthropic and OpenAI, shows similar slippage. For Anthropic, the price per million tokens went from $2.65 on May 1, 2026 to $0.62 on October 22, 2026, a decline of 77 percent. In a message shared with Darkbloom participants on the company's Slack channel, Kydo, one of the Eigen Labs researchers working on the distributed inference network, celebrated the network's processing of its trillionth token while attempting to moderate expectations about the project's viability. "Earnings have been low," said Kydo. "For most providers, I don't expect that it is going to recover soon." Pointing to the computational prowess of DeekSeek's DeepInfer framework , he explained that structural changes in the inference market have affected the supply of tokens. "Data centers have become cheaper," he said. "Output per NVIDIA cluster is up ~20x this year, and their margins are wide enough to cut prices 90 percent and still profit at 50 percent." The flood of tokens in turn has washed away the price advantage Darkbloom had previously. "The market caught up to our price," Kydo explained. "We could go lower, but then most of you would earn even less nothing." Finally, he said, the inference routing market is changing, with OpenRouter moving away from price-based routing and putting more emphasis on decode speed, quantization, and prefill speed. For network participants with older or less powerful Mac hardware – those without top of the line Max or Ultra Apple Silicon – "inference won't be worth running," he said. Kydo went on to outline

item.title: India launches next-gen navigation satellite to orbit (video)
item.description: null India bolstered its homegrown satellite-navigation system today (Oct. 30). A GSLV Mark II rocket launched the nation's NVS-03 satellite from Satish Dhawan Space Centre today at 2:21 p.m. EDT (1821 GMT and 11:51 p.m. India Standard Time). Everything went well: The rocket deployed NVS-03 into geostationary transfer orbit as planned, officials with the Indian Space Research Organisation (ISRO) announced on X about 30 minutes after liftoff. An Indian GSLV Mark II rocket launches the NVS-03 navigation satellite on Oct. 30, 2026. (Image credit: ISRO) NVS-03 is the third next-gen satellite that India has launched for the Navigation with Indian Constellation (NavIC), its version of the United States' Global Positioning System ( GPS ). NavIC operates on a smaller scale than its American counterpart, however. It's "a regional navigation satellite system designed to provide accurate Position, Navigation and Timing (PNT) service to users in India as well as the region extending about 1,500 km [930 miles] beyond the Indian landmass, which is its primary service area," ISRO officials wrote in the NVS-03 launch brochure . The Indian constellation currently consists of three fully functioning satellites, and it requires four to provide PNT services. So today's launch was a big deal — and a lot of eyes will be watching NVS-03's commissioning and checkout phase. Today's launch was the 14th to date for the GSLV (Geosynchronous Satellite Launch Vehicle) Mark II, a three-stage rocket that stands 170 feet (52 meters) tall. Twelve of those 14 liftoffs have been successful. The GSLV Mark II debuted in 2010, the same year its predecessor retired. That previous launchers, the Mark I, flew a total of six times, with two failures. NVS-03 was the fourth Indian launch of 2026 and the third operated by ISRO. The fourth was mounted by Skyroot Aerospace, which in July became the first Indian company ever to successfully reach orbit .

item.title: Over 25% of people lie to get antibiotics—and their lies aren't even good
item.description: A significant number of patients in the US lie to their doctors to get antibiotics they likely don't need, according to two new studies. While that may not be a startling revelation, the studies drills down on the phenomenon, finding that the lies patients tell are generally bad ones—and yet, they work almost all the time. In the two linked studies published Friday in JAMA Network Open, a team of researchers led by Alistair Thorpe at the University of Utah analyzed online survey data from over 1,000 adults. They found that over a quarter of people reported having lied to a clinician at least once to get an antibiotic prescription for themselves or a child in their care. Patients lied by either exaggerating symptoms, making up symptoms, or—most often—both. But interestingly, the lies people told to get antibiotics involved making up or exaggerating symptoms of infections that wouldn't be treated with antibiotics. For example, the most common falsehoods were symptoms associated with colds, such as fever, cough, and sore throat. That's despite the fact that colds are caused by viruses, not bacteria—which antibiotics treat. Read full article Comments

item.title: HTTP/3 is faster with some work and help from Cloudflare
item.description: When you're ordering food from your phone, even time spent navigating the app is time wasted. At the P99 2026 virtual conference , Elvis Chidera , a staff engineer at Germany-based global delivery service Delivery Hero , explained how the company moved most of its user base to HTTP/3, and consequently cut its apps’ total end-to-end response time of the home screen by 17 percent. Chidera, who managed the project, explained that, as promised on the tin, HTTP/3 delivers the web faster than HTTP/2, though it has slow bits that need to be adjusted to work properly. Uber eats Delivery Hero Delivery Hero is all but unknown in the US, which is dominated by Uber Eats and DoorDash. But it is a company with global reach outside the US, with an estimated user base of 60 million across Europe, Latin America, Africa, the Middle East, and Asia. Uber is currently acquiring Delivery Hero for $14.8 billion, with plans to unite the company with Uber Eats. With this purchase, Uber would expand the number of markets where it offers both ride-hailing and delivery services, though not necessarily under the Uber Eats nameplate. Delivery Hero centrally manages separate apps for different regions, all of which it built or acquired. Asians can order poke bowls and sundries through Foodpanda . Turks can order kebabs through Yemeksepeti . Throughout Spain, Italy, Poland, Romania, Ukraine, and much of Africa, the Glovo app is where to ring up the late-night deliveries. And in Latin America, users dial in to PedidosYa to get what they need from nearby farmacias, restaurantes, and mercados. All these regions have widely varying network connectivity, a problem Delivery Hero wanted to minimize. Last mile networking was most often the bottleneck. Apps in Pakistan, for instance, could take nearly a second (at p90) to establish a secure handshake with a server. The engineering team looked at HTTP/3 as a way to lower, even eliminate, that latency. A QUIC-er HTTP The Internet Engineering Task Force (IETF) formally introduced the third version of the internet’s Hypertext Transfer Protocol in 2022. HTTP is the application layer protocol that connects browsers and other resources connected to servers over the Internet. The previous versions of HTTP were built on the Transmission Control Protocol (TCP), which offered guaranteed delivery and flow control. In conjunction with the Internet Protocol (IP), TCP/IP built the modern internet. HTTP/3 replaced TCP with Quick UDP Internet Connection (QUIC), developed by Google , to address some of TCP’s p erceived sluggishness as a transfer protocol. UDP stands for User Datagram Protocol and, unlike TCP, it does not guarantee packet delivery or flow control. UDP is faster because it doesn’t wait around for a signature (QUIC adds in its own flow control on top of UDP). But the UDP-based HTTP/3 reduces, and sometimes eliminates, the round trips needed to secure connections. The app can cache a session ticket and, on a later connection, use QUIC's 0-RT
